title: Homo Fluxus: A Thermodynamic Framework for Consciousness, Systemic Empathy, and Aligned Intelligence
description: Proposes a thermodynamic substrate for cognition in which local entropy minimization via coherent information flow underlies consciousness, affect, ethics, and AI alignment. Introduces Homo Fluxus (agent-as-node-in-flow) and systemic empathy (field-coupled coherence sensitivity), and specifies operational proxies for a coherence potential with falsifiable, cross-scale predictions.

local_entropy_reduction_condition.description: When local entropy decreases, energy flow aligns with the gradient of the coherence potential; coherent flow drives local entropy reduction.

coherence_proxy_mapping.description: At the cognitive scale, the coherence potential projects onto a low-dimensional latent factor jointly reflected in integrated information rate, cross-frequency phase coherence, and interoceptive–allostatic integration.

key_results.main_finding: Defines Homo Fluxus and systemic empathy as consequences of an EFC-based coherence potential, proposes measurable proxies that must co-vary as a single latent factor, and outlines falsifiable predictions linking consciousness, affect, cooperation, and alignment.

sealed_predictions.statement: A single latent coherence factor will be recoverable that co-varies monotonically across integrated information rate, cross-frequency phase coherence, and interoceptive–allostatic integration, with consistent temporal alignment across modalities during coherence transitions (e.g., anesthesia, sleep–wake, meditation).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Simultaneous EEG/MEG + autonomic/interoceptive (e.g., ECG, respiration) + behavioral reports across controlled state transitions; failure to recover a cross-modal, cross-condition latent factor invalidates the claim.

sealed_predictions.statement: Increasing interoceptive/field coupling (e.g., via slow breathing, vagal stimulation, or interoceptive training) will increase the latent coherence factor and measurably shift action weighting toward extra-boundary state (systemic empathy) in social decision tasks.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Randomized controlled trials combining VNS or paced respiration with EEG/MEG/ANS recordings and economic games (public goods, commons dilemmas); absence of predicted joint shifts refutes the mechanism.

sealed_predictions.statement: In multi-agent computational settings, adding a field-coupling term that approximates \nabla\Phi_coh to local objectives will produce scalable cooperative equilibria; removing the term reverts to extractive/local optima.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Ablation studies in MARL benchmarks comparing cooperation metrics with and without explicit coupling terms; lack of differential effect falsifies the alignment implication.

kill_criteria: KC1: Across controlled state transitions (e.g., anesthesia induction/emergence, sleep–wake, meditation), no recoverable cross-modal latent factor jointly loading on integrated information rate, cross-frequency phase coherence, and interoceptive–allostatic integration, or inconsistent temporal alignment of such a factor across modalities and conditions.

KC2: Robust evidence that increases in the proposed coherence proxies are repeatedly accompanied by estimated violations of Eq. (1) (i.e., the empirical estimate of Ef · ∇Φcoh is non-positive) beyond methodological uncertainty, using pre-registered proxy-to-variable mappings.

KC3: Sustained experimental dissociations in which Φ̇I, Cphase, and Ibody can be independently driven in opposing directions for extended periods without converging or affecting reported conscious level, contradicting the single-variable projection claim.

KC4: Interventions that measurably increase field/interoceptive coupling (e.g., VNS, slow breathing) fail to produce any increase in extra-boundary weighting (systemic empathy) in pre-registered social decision tasks across adequately powered samples.

KC5: Demonstration of scalable alignment in open-world AI systems achieved by purely local optimizers without any field-coupling or extra-boundary terms, across tasks where coupled externalities are measurable, contradicting the posited structural failure mode.

KC6: Cross-laboratory replications show that the proposed proxies do not co-vary or that their relationship is best explained by independent factors rather than a common latent variable tied to a thermodynamic coherence construct.
